text:
The roosters will sing when we die,

and a light breeze, with delicate hands,

will brush the edges, the

funereal silks.

And the sound of night will transpire

over the clear panes.

And crickets in the distance will break the silences,

the crystal stalks, cold, long, barren,

and the immense fragrance of the trees.

Ah, what sweet moon will see our calm

face calmer still than its great mirror

of silver!

What dense coolness in our hair,

free as fields at dawn!

In the mist of daybreak

the last star

rises pale.

What great stillness, without human speech,

without the lip of wolves’ faces,

without hate, without love, without anything!

Like dark lost prophets,

dogs in the countryside will barely converse.

Strong questions. Vast pauses.

We shall be in death

with that gentle outline

of a shell beneath the water.

translation.title: The Roosters Will Sing
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish version of a Portuguese original; its contemplative, segmented verse is preserved.
